tls-server-verifier.task: Build rustls's WebPKI server verifier over a Linux distribution bundle, or verify a captured origin chain and name with it; bundle parsing is untimed.

openssl-hashes.task: Hash one buffer through the production one-shot API, including context construction and destruction.

openssl-hashes-streaming.task: Construct a digest context, hash 1 MiB in the named chunk size, finalize and destroy the context.

openssl-aes-gcm.task: Construct a fresh key/context, then seal or authenticate and open one message into preallocated output; include production API copies and context destruction.

ecdsa-verify-der-reuse.task: Parse the same DER signature, hash and verify the message with a parsed public key reused across calls; ring has no parsed-key API.

ecdsa-verify-der-import.task: Import the same uncompressed SEC1 key, parse the same DER signature, hash and verify the message.

blake2-params.task: Construct parameters, then hash with the same salt, personalization and output length.

quic-handshakes.task: Complete both QUIC v1 TLS handshakes and traffic-key derivation through raw TLS events; include allocation, copies and destruction. Configuration and key import are untimed.

quic-packets.task: Protect or authenticate one 1-RTT payload with retained keys and storage, including buffer restoration and packet-number handling. Sizes and throughput count plaintext bytes.

quic-headers.task: Apply or remove production QUIC header protection for a short header, four-byte packet number and 16-byte sample using retained keys.

quinn-connections.task: Complete both Quinn endpoints through in-memory UDP, including allocation, immediate control traffic and destruction. TLS varies by provider; the shared adapter always uses rscrypto for Initial, Retry and token cryptography.

tls-handshakes.task: Complete the named TLS 1.3 handshake on both endpoints, including connection construction, transport copies, ticket processing and destruction; configuration and key import are untimed.

tls-traffic.task: Encrypt, transport, authenticate and copy application bytes on a reused connection; the size is per direction, and bidirectional throughput counts both directions.

crc.task: Checksum one buffer in one call.

crc-streaming.task: Checksum 1 MiB through updates of the named chunk size.

crc-combine.task: Combine the checksums of two parts, given the length of the second part.

sha2.task: Hash one buffer in one call.

sha2-streaming.task: Hash 1 MiB through updates of the named chunk size.

sha3.task: Hash one buffer in one call.

sha3-streaming.task: Hash 1 MiB through updates of the named chunk size.

shake.task: Absorb one buffer and squeeze 32 bytes in one call.

shake-xof-output.task: Absorb a 32-byte seed and squeeze the named output length.

kmac.task: Absorb the key, customization, and one message, then finalize a 32-byte tag.

cshake.task: Absorb the function name, customization, and one message, then squeeze 32 bytes.

hmac-sha3.task: Tag one message with a key prepared once.

ascon-hash.task: Hash one buffer in one call.

blake2.task: Hash one buffer in one call.

blake2-keyed.task: Keyed hash of one buffer in one call.

blake2-short-oneshot.task: Hash one short buffer in one call.

blake2-short-keyed.task: Keyed hash of one short buffer in one call.

blake2-streaming.task: Hash through updates of the named chunk size.

xxh3.task: Hash one buffer in one call. Each competitor counts with its fastest supported build.

xxh3-baseline-build.task: Hash one buffer in one call. Every library uses the default build, so compile-time-only SIMD stays at the target baseline.

xxh3-v4-build.task: Hash one buffer in one call. Every crate is compiled for x86-64-v4.

xxh3-buildhasher.task: Hash one byte slice through the collection hasher.

xxh3-hashmap.task: Look up keys in a hash map built with the collection hasher.

rapidhash.task: Hash one buffer in one call with RapidHash V3.

rapidhash-stream.task: Hash one buffer through the streaming hasher.

rapidhash-buildhasher.task: Hash one byte slice through the collection hasher.

rapidhash-hash-one.task: Hash one value through the collection hasher.

rapidhash-hashmap.task: Insert or look up keys in a hash map built with the collection hasher.

poly1305.task: Authenticate one message with a one-time key, including key setup and finalization.

hmac-sha2.task: Tag one message with a key prepared once.

hmac-sha2-streaming.task: Key, then tag a message through updates of the named chunk size.

hmac-sha2-verify-reuse.task: Verify one tag over a message with a key prepared once.

hmac-sha2-verify-import.task: Key from bytes, then verify one tag over a message.

hkdf-expand.task: Expand a pseudorandom key prepared once to the named output length.

hkdf-extract.task: Extract a pseudorandom key from a salt and input keying material of the named length.

pbkdf2.task: Derive the named output length from a password and salt.

pbkdf2-verify.task: Derive a key at the password-policy iteration count and compare it with a stored key.

argon2.task: Derive 32 raw bytes from a password and a 16-byte salt, with scratch allocation and cleanup timed.

argon2-reused-memory.task: Derive 32 raw bytes into work memory allocated once outside timing.

scrypt.task: Derive raw bytes from a password and salt, with scratch allocation and cleanup timed.

slhdsa-keygen.task: Generate a key pair from fixed seeds.

slhdsa-sign.task: Sign a 32-byte message deterministically with a reused key.

slhdsa-verify.task: Verify one signature with a reused key.

slhdsa-hash-sign.task: HashSLH-DSA: sign a 32-byte message deterministically with a reused key.

slhdsa-hash-verify.task: HashSLH-DSA: verify one signature with a reused key.

aead-encrypt.task: Restore the message into a reused buffer, then encrypt it with a reused cipher context.

aead-decrypt.task: Restore the ciphertext into a reused buffer, then decrypt and verify it with a reused cipher context.

aes-siv.task: Restore the input into a reused buffer, then seal or open it with a reused cipher.

aes-siv-construct.task: Construct a cipher, restore the input, and seal it.

aead-construct-encrypt.task: Encrypt one message under a new key: build a cipher from key bytes, restore the input, encrypt it, and destroy the cipher.

header-protection-mask.task: Compute one five-byte RFC 9001 header-protection mask with a context built once.

header-protection-construct.task: Build a header-protection context from key bytes, then destroy it.

blake3-hash.task: Hash one buffer in one call on one thread.

blake3-keyed.task: Keyed-hash one buffer in one call on one thread.

blake3-derive-key.task: Derive a key, hashing the context string in each call, on one thread.

blake3-derive-key-prepared.task: Derive a key from a context hashed before timing, on one thread.

blake3-xof.task: Absorb one buffer and squeeze 64 bytes on one thread.

blake3-xof-output.task: Absorb a 32-byte seed and squeeze the named output length on one thread.

blake3-bao-decode.task: Verify and decode a whole Bao combined encoding from memory against a trusted root, on one thread.

blake3-ordered.task: Hash or derive from one buffer through the named call shape, on one thread.

blake3-ordered-alignment.task: The ordered task with input addresses congruent to 0 or 1 modulo 64.

blake3-parallel-hash.task: Hash one buffer in one call; threads allowed.

blake3-parallel-keyed.task: Keyed-hash one buffer in one call; threads allowed.

blake3-parallel-derive-key.task: Derive a key, hashing the context string in each call; threads allowed.

blake3-parallel-xof.task: Absorb one buffer and squeeze 64 bytes; threads allowed.

blake3-streaming.task: Hash 1 MiB through updates of the named chunk size.

blake3-batch.task: Hash 64 independent messages of the named length.

blake3-mixed-batch.task: Hash an ordered list of independent messages of mixed lengths.

mldsa-keygen.task: Generate a key pair from a 32-byte seed and export both encoded keys.

mldsa-sign-deterministic.task: Sign a 32-byte message deterministically with an empty context and each library's best reused key.

mldsa-sign-randomized.task: Sign a 32-byte message with 32 fresh random bytes, an empty context, and each library's best reused key.

mldsa-verify-reuse.task: Parse and verify one signature with an empty context and each library's best reused key.

mldsa-verify-import.task: Import identical public-key bytes, then parse and verify one signature with an empty context.

mldsa-sign-encoded.task: Sign deterministically with an 18-byte context and a key that is decoded in each call.

mldsa-sign-prepared.task: Sign deterministically with an 18-byte context and a key prepared once.

mldsa-verify-encoded.task: Verify with an 18-byte context and a key that is decoded in each call.

mldsa-verify-prepared.task: Verify with an 18-byte context and a key prepared once.

mldsa-corpus.task: Sign each message of a fixed corpus with a prepared key, deterministically or hedged.

mldsa-hash-sign.task: HashML-DSA with SHAKE128: sign deterministically with a key decoded in each call.

mldsa-hash-verify.task: HashML-DSA with SHAKE128: verify with a key decoded in each call.

rsa-verify-reuse.task: Verify one SHA-256 signature with a public key prepared once, through each library's best reuse API.

rsa-verify-import.task: Parse and validate identical PKCS#1 public-key bytes, then verify one SHA-256 signature.

rsa-parse-spki.task: Parse and validate identical SubjectPublicKeyInfo bytes.

rsa-parse-spki-8192.task: Parse and validate identical 8192-bit SubjectPublicKeyInfo bytes.
rsa-parse-spki-8192.availability: Only AWS-LC supplies an external 8192-bit SPKI parser; this suite excludes it on IBM Z. RustCrypto's parser stops at 4096 bits, and ring has no public RSA SPKI parser.

rsa-sign.task: Sign with PSS or PKCS #1 v1.5 and SHA-256, using fresh salt or blinding randomness in each call, with a private key prepared once.

rsa-oaep-encrypt.task: Encrypt one message with OAEP and SHA-256 using fresh randomness in each call.

rsa-oaep-encrypt-caller-entropy.task: Encrypt one message with OAEP and SHA-256 using a seed that the caller supplies.

rsa-oaep-decrypt.task: Decrypt one OAEP SHA-256 ciphertext with fresh blinding randomness in each call.

rsa-pkcs1v15-decrypt.task: Decrypt one legacy RSAES-PKCS1-v1_5 ciphertext with fresh blinding randomness in each call.

rsa-keygen.task: Generate a key pair. Prime search makes the time vary widely between calls.

ecdsa-sign.task: Sign a message of the named length with a private key prepared once.

ecdsa-verify-reuse.task: Verify one signature with a public key parsed once, through each library's best reuse API.

ecdsa-verify-import.task: Parse identical uncompressed SEC1 public-key bytes, then verify one signature.

ecdsa-public-key.task: Derive the public key from a private key held by the caller.

ecdsa-signature-der.task: Encode a parsed signature as DER, or parse and validate a DER signature.

ed25519-sign.task: Sign a message of the named length with a key pair prepared once.

ed25519-verify-reuse.task: Verify one signature with a public key parsed once, through each library's best reuse API.

ed25519-verify-import.task: Import identical 32-byte public-key bytes, then verify one signature.

ed25519-key-derivation.task: Derive the public key or the signing key pair from a 32-byte secret.

x25519-diffie-hellman.task: Compute one shared secret from a reused secret key and the peer's encoded 32-byte public key.

x25519-public-key.task: Derive the public key from a 32-byte secret key.

ecdh-key-generation.task: Generate a key pair from caller-supplied randomness.

ecdh-agreement-parsed-peer.task: Compute one shared secret from a reused private key and a peer public key parsed once.

ecdh-agreement-encoded-peer.task: Parse identical SEC1 peer bytes, then compute one shared secret with a reused private key.

ecdh-public-key.task: Derive the public key from a private key held by the caller.

ecdh-public-key-from-secret.task: Import secret-key bytes, then derive the public key.

ecdh-parse.task: Parse and validate identical SEC1 public-key bytes.

mlkem-keygen.task: Generate a key pair from a 64-byte seed and export both encoded keys.

mlkem-encapsulate-reuse.task: Encapsulate with caller randomness and each library's best reused key.

mlkem-encapsulate-import.task: Import and validate identical encapsulation-key bytes, then encapsulate with caller randomness.

mlkem-decapsulate-reuse.task: Decapsulate one ciphertext with each library's best reused key.

mlkem-decapsulate-import.task: Import and validate identical decapsulation-key bytes, then decapsulate one ciphertext.

mlkem-reuse-encoded.task: Encapsulate or decapsulate with a reused encoded-key wrapper that decodes the key in each call.
